Koh Samui's two best-known wellness resorts are Kamalaya at Laem Set in the south-east, with programmes from about US$1,836 for 3 nights to about US$4,954 for 7 nights including 10% service and 7% VAT, and Absolute Sanctuary near Choeng Mon, 5 minutes from the airport, with 6-night programmes from about US$2,152 nett. Samahita on Laem Sor beach is the budget all-inclusive option at about US$654 per person for 3 nights. For a lighter reset, Tamarind Springs' forest spa (from 1,500 THB++) and resort day passes (from 1,800 THB++ in 2026) work without an overnight stay.

Dollar prices are the resorts' own conversions from Thai baht and move with the exchange rate. Room category, season and single occupancy change the final price. We name these resorts for orientation; we don't link to them or take commission on stays.

Kamalaya

Kamalaya is a hillside wellness resort on Laem Set Road in Na Mueang, about 25 km (45 minutes) from the airport. The resort is built around a cave once used by Buddhist monks for meditation [check]. It offers structured programmes with a wellness consultation, a body-composition analysis, daily holistic activities, treatments and nutrition. Facilities include herbal steam caverns, thermal plunge pools, swimming pools and the Shakti fitness centre. Since 1 April 2026, breakfast is included in room rates.

First-time guests staying fewer than 7 nights must book at least a 3-night wellness programme. In 2026 Kamalaya also sold day passes open to all travellers, from 1,800 THB++ (wellness day with a holistic activity) to 5,300 THB++ (with a spa treatment), and an early-booking discount of 10–20% for stays of 8 nights or more booked 60 days ahead. Offers change with the season, so check current terms before booking.

Absolute Sanctuary

Absolute Sanctuary is a wellness resort at 88 Moo 5, Choeng Mon, about 5 minutes from the airport and 5 minutes from Chaweng. It has three yoga spaces and a studio, a Pilates reformer studio, a detox and spa centre, a juice bar and the Love Kitchen restaurant, which focuses on plant-rich, healthy food. Samahita and Vikasa: yoga-led and better value

Samahita Retreat sits directly on Laem Sor beach on the quiet south coast. Its 3-, 5- and 7-day programmes include a room, a yoga and fitness schedule, buffet meals, a saltwater pool, float therapy, evening herbal steam and one spa treatment, from about US$654 per person sharing for 3 nights including service and VAT. It suits people who want to train and eat well rather than follow a medical-style programme.

Vikasa on the cliffs between Chaweng Noi and Coral Cove is primarily a yoga retreat: a 7-day stay with unlimited classes, brunch and dinner costs from about US$1,030, and it also runs personal programmes including a "Vitox" detox week. More on both in our yoga guide.

Spa resorts and day spas

If you want treatments rather than a programme, Samui's luxury resorts, among them Six Senses Samui on the north-east tip, Banyan Tree on the headland near Lamai and the Four Seasons at Laem Yai, have full-service spas that take outside bookings. The standout day spa is Tamarind Springs in the Thong Takian hills behind Lamai, open 09:00–18:00, with herbal steam caves and plunge pools among the boulders: Steam and Dream costs 1,500 THB++ per person, and packages with a 2.5-hour massage start at 5,500 THB++. Shop and spa prices across the island are in our spa and massage guide.

Types of programmes

  • Detox and fasting: juice or plant-based menus, supplements, colon or lymphatic treatments and steam. Expect tiredness and headaches for the first 2–3 days.
  • Fitness and weight management: personal training, Pilates, Muay Thai or HIIT, body-composition tracking and calorie-controlled menus.
  • Sleep and stress: consultations, relaxation therapies, breathwork, yoga nidra and digital curfews.
  • Yoga and mindfulness: daily classes, meditation and workshops; see meditation on Koh Samui.
  • Ayurveda and traditional medicine: Ayurvedic consultations and treatments, Thai herbal compresses and steam.
  • Structural and recovery: posture, physiotherapy-style bodywork and massage for back and joint problems.

A typical day on a wellness programme

Each resort sets its own schedule; this is the usual shape of a day on a Samui detox or balance programme.

  1. 07:00 Morning yoga, qigong or a guided walk; a detox drink or light breakfast.
  2. 09:00 Consultation or check-in with your therapist or coach.
  3. 10:00 Treatment: massage, lymphatic drainage, herbal compress or a body wrap.
  4. 12:30 Lunch from the programme menu, or juice on a cleanse.
  5. 14:00 Free time: pool, rest, reading or a workshop.
  6. 16:00 Fitness or Pilates session, then herbal steam and a plunge pool.
  7. 18:30 Light dinner and an early night.

Questions to ask before you book

  • What exactly is included each day, and which treatments cost extra?
  • Who leads the consultations, and what are their qualifications?
  • Is the price per person or per room, and does it include service charge and VAT?
  • What is the minimum stay for my programme and room type?
  • What are the deposit and cancellation terms, and what happens if I fall ill?
  • Are airport transfers included, and how far is the resort from the airport?
  • Can the menu handle allergies, vegan diets or medical diets?

Medical cautions

Wellness programmes are not medical treatment, and some detox elements carry real risks. Talk to your own doctor before booking if any of these apply:

  • You take regular medication, especially for diabetes, blood pressure, heart conditions, epilepsy or mental health; fasting and juice diets can change how drugs work and how your body handles them.
  • You are pregnant or breastfeeding, have an eating disorder history, kidney or liver disease, or are underweight.
  • You plan colon hydrotherapy and have bowel disease or recent abdominal surgery.
  • You plan steam and heat treatments with a heart condition or low blood pressure.

Tell the resort's consultant everything at your first consultation, and stop any treatment that makes you feel faint or unwell. Samui's private hospitals are 10–45 minutes away depending on the resort; see hospitals on Koh Samui.

What it really costs, and what "++" means

  • "++": Thai hotel and spa prices often exclude a 10% service charge and 7% VAT, adding about 17.7% to the listed price. Kamalaya's programme prices above already include both; Absolute Sanctuary lists its prices as nett; check day-pass and à la carte menus.
  • Single supplements: programme prices are usually per person sharing, or for a room; solo travellers pay more.
  • Extras: airport transfers, additional treatments, alcohol (if allowed), laundry and excursions are often extra.
  • Season: rates rise from mid-December to April and fall from May to October.
  • Flights: most guests fly via Bangkok; one-way fares from Bangkok to Samui run about 2,800–6,800 THB.

Best season for a wellness retreat

PeriodWhat to expect

A resort programme or a DIY wellness week?

A DIY week works well from a quiet base such as Lamai (close to Tamarind Springs and good-value massage) or Choeng Mon. The south, with Bang Kao and Laem Set, is the quietest part of the island. All options are listed on the retreats hub.

After your programme

Ease back into normal food gradually for a few days after a detox, keep up the habits you started (morning movement, sleep times, water) and book a follow-up with your own doctor if the programme recommended one. If you have a few days left on Samui, a quiet base such as Choeng Mon or Lamai and a daily massage keep the benefits going longer than a jump straight into Chaweng's nightlife.

Light boat days to add

A gentle day on the water fits most programmes on a rest day.

  • Boutique yachting day: Ang Thong on a 30 m wooden gulet with breakfast and lunch, park fee included, 4,500 THB (from 16 December).
  • Sunset cruises: from the shared Pig Island sunset tour at 1,550 THB to a private sailing catamaran from 20,000 THB per boat.
  • Pig Island speedboat: a half day with snorkelling at Koh Tan, 1,450 THB, every day of the year.

Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui. Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut (and other remote areas) add 400 THB per person, return; south-coast resorts should check the zone on each product page.
